overall_notes: Pregame NBA-heavy slate with two same-game clusters (NY@IND, MEM@NO) where I'd avoid stacking. I kept legs with clearer role/injury tailwinds and softer books, and cut thin-margin shooting props, blowout-sensitive overs, and Wagner TO after Suggs' likely return. App line confirmation still matters for several FGM markets.

votes.reasoning: Coward's recent rebounding run plus Memphis frontcourt absences and a high total point to extra missed shots and board share. New Orleans' interior doubts add a bit more upside. I'd flip if Coward's minutes or starting role shrinks in late injury reports.

Towns' sustained double-double streak and Indiana's weak center defense are a solid matchup fit with Haliburton out. The main drag is a potential NY blowout trimming fourth-quarter usage. A tighter spread or Nesmith playing heavy minutes on a hot night would lower my edge.

Books are unusually aggressive on Stone over 1.5 SOG, which usually reflects real volume expectation at home. Nashville's stingy shot suppression is the honest pushback on a low bar prop. I'd cut if Stone is limited or Vegas is a heavy underdog game script.

The hit rate looks great but many games land on exactly five makes, so 4.5 is a knife-edge line against a very efficient -190 price. Mobley out helps less for a guard's make count than the drafter implies, and FGM availability on pick'em apps is unverified. I'd keep only if the app line drops meaningfully below books.

Haliburton out boosts usage but 4.5 FGM with repeated scores of exactly five is fragile, and the last five is only 4/5 over. Stacking with Towns in the same game adds correlation if pace or shooting goes cold. Clearer green light if the line were 3.5 or books were softer.

2.5 FGM is a more forgiving bar with strong recent clears and a guard-heavy Memphis rotation when bigs are out. The book at roughly -125 doesn't scream misprice, so the bet is mostly trend plus pace. Shorter rotation or a slower-than-expected total would worry me.

Toppin's recent PRA clears are encouraging but he's still a bench piece in a likely Knicks blowout, which caps minutes and counting stats. Nesmith's status adds noise to the minutes story rather than a clean boost. I'd reconsider if the spread tightens materially pre-tip.

Season average and projection barely clear 11.5, and he's ticked 11 twice in the last six—classic one-rebound short. Golden State's absences help missed shots but a Spurs blowout could limit Wemby's fourth quarter. Fox or Vassell sitting changes context but doesn't fix the efficient line.

Usage and season PRA support the idea but Portland as a double-digit dog raises early bench risk and he's gone 32 and 29 lately—both under 34.5. The prior Portland game helps narrative more than a repeatable path tonight. I'd keep if Sacramento's spread tightens or the pick'em line drops.

The 10-game TO streak is real but Suggs likely returning meaningfully shares primary creation and reduces Wagner's burden. The morning downgrade in the drafter's own notes aligns with cutting this on a 2.5 line that needs three turnovers. I'd only revisit if Suggs is ruled out close to tip.
